fields.label: User
fields.description: One field user per login. The login must already hold a FieldMate role.

fields.label: Mobile No
fields.description: Filled from the login, or from the Employee record if the login has no number, whenever this is left blank. Type one here only where the rep's work number differs from both - what is typed is never overwritten.

fields.label: Employee
fields.description: Links attendance and expense claims to HR when that is in use, and fills Company and Joining Date below. Setting it also lets the journey planner read that employee's Holiday List, so a planned day never lands on a holiday.

fields.label: Designation
fields.options:
Field Rep
Area Manager
Regional Manager
Sales Head

fields.label: Status
fields.description: Inactive removes territory access without deleting history.

fields.label: Territory
fields.description: Drives row-level access. Territory is a tree, so a manager placed on a parent node sees everything beneath it.

fields.label: Node in the Target Tree
fields.description: Where this rep sits in the sales hierarchy, as an ERPNext Sales Person. This is the ONLY thing it is for: an area target is split down this tree and achievement is rolled back up it, so a rep who is not on it gets no share of a plan and appears in no roll-up. It is not a person record and not a permission - the login, the territory and the manager are the three fields above. Leave it empty only for somebody no target will ever reach.

fields.label: Company
fields.description: Taken from the Employee record, on every save - HR owns which company somebody is employed by, so a rep whose Employee record moves follows it. While an Employee is linked a company set by hand here WILL be replaced on the next save; to choose one yourself, clear the Employee link above. With no Employee it falls back to the default company.

fields.label: Distributor
fields.description: The billing party this rep sells through.

fields.label: Can Onboard Outlets
fields.description: New outlets still land in Pending Approval.

fields.label: Can Collect Payment
fields.description: Collecting is not posting. A Payment Entry is still only created on deposit confirmation.

fields.label: Daily Calls When There Is No Route
fields.description: The fallback only. On a planned day the target is the number of shops on the beat the journey plan names for that day, which moves with the plan - a short Thursday beat asks for less than a long Monday one. This figure is used where there is no plan for the day, or on a site that works to a flat expectation instead. It shipped with a default of 25, so every rep on every site was asked for 25 calls whether their beat held 12 shops or 60 and nobody had chosen it; the default is gone, and empty now honestly means nobody has set one.

fields.label: Joining Date
fields.description: Taken from the Employee record where there is one. Only fills a blank. It is the date the rep joined, not the date the app was given to them - incentive slabs that count months of service read this.

fields.label: What This Rep Covers
fields.description: Counted by the app, never typed. Nothing here is a setting - it is what the masters already say about this rep, gathered in one place so a manager does not have to go looking.

fields.label: Beats Assigned
fields.description: How many beats name this rep.

fields.label: Outlets On Those Beats
fields.description: Shops across those beats. This is the number a daily call target should be set against.

fields.label: Phone Last Synced
fields.description: When this rep's handset last reached the server. A date several days old means their work is sitting on the phone and nobody has it - which is the one thing on this form worth checking every morning.
